---
title: "Jansen-Rit Spectral Fitting via tvboptim"
---

This example shows how to define a **complete simulation & optimization experiment** entirely as TVBO metadata using `SimulationExperiment.from_string()`. Everything—equations, parameters, integration, coupling, observation pipeline, target data, and loss function—is specified inline in a single YAML string.

The information below mirrors the [JR.qmd tutorial](https://github.com/virtual-twin/tvboptim/blob/main/docs/workflows/JR.qmd) from tvboptim.

## Full Experiment as TVBO Metadata

```{python}
from tvbo import SimulationExperiment

experiment_yaml = """
# SimulationExperiment requires 'id' (integer identifier)
id: 1
label: "JR Peak Frequency Optimization"
description: >
  Reproducing MEG Resting-State Frequency Gradients with Network Dynamics.
  This experiment fits region-specific Jansen-Rit parameters to reproduce
  the empirical frequency gradient from visual cortex (11 Hz) to association
  areas (7 Hz).

# --------------------------------------------------------
# LOCAL DYNAMICS: Jansen-Rit Neural Mass Model (6-dimensional)
# From tvboptim.experimental.network_dynamics.dynamics.tvb.JansenRit
# --------------------------------------------------------
local_dynamics:
  name: JansenRit
  label: "Jansen-Rit Neural Mass Model"
  description: >
    Neural mass model with three populations (pyramidal, excitatory interneurons,
    inhibitory interneurons). Produces characteristic alpha-band oscillations.

  # --- PARAMETERS (from JansenRit.DEFAULT_PARAMS in JR.qmd) ---
  parameters:
    A:
      value: 3.25
      description: "Maximum amplitude of EPSP [mV]"
      unit: mV
    B:
      value: 22.0
      description: "Maximum amplitude of IPSP [mV]"
      unit: mV
    a:
      value: 0.065
      description: "Reciprocal of membrane time constant (excitatory)"
      domain: {lo: 0.001, hi: 0.2}
      unit: ms^-1
      free: true
      heterogeneous: true
    b:
      value: 0.065
      description: "Reciprocal of membrane time constant (inhibitory)"
      domain: {lo: 0.001, hi: 0.2}
      unit: ms^-1
      free: true
      heterogeneous: true
    v0:
      value: 5.52
      description: "Firing threshold [mV]"
      unit: mV
    nu_max:
      value: 0.0025
      description: "Maximum firing rate"
      unit: ms^-1
    r:
      value: 0.56
      description: "Steepness of sigmoid"
      unit: mV^-1
    J:
      value: 135.0
      description: "Average number of synapses"
    a_1:
      value: 1.0
      description: "Excitatory feedback probability"
    a_2:
      value: 0.8
      description: "Slow excitatory feedback probability"
    a_3:
      value: 0.25
      description: "Inhibitory feedback probability"
    a_4:
      value: 0.25
      description: "Slow inhibitory feedback probability"
    mu:
      value: 0.15
      description: "Mean input firing rate"

  # --- DERIVED VARIABLES (sigmoid activations) ---
  derived_variables:
    sigm_y1_y2:
      equation:
        rhs: "2.0 * nu_max / (1.0 + exp(r * (v0 - (y1 - y2))))"
      description: "Sigmoid of y1-y2"
    sigm_y0_1:
      equation:
        rhs: "2.0 * nu_max / (1.0 + exp(r * (v0 - (a_1 * J * y0))))"
      description: "Sigmoid of a_1*J*y0"
    sigm_y0_3:
      equation:
        rhs: "2.0 * nu_max / (1.0 + exp(r * (v0 - (a_3 * J * y0))))"
      description: "Sigmoid of a_3*J*y0"

  # --- STATE VARIABLES (6D system) ---
  state_variables:
    y0:
      equation:
        rhs: "y3"
      initial_value: 0.0
    y1:
      equation:
        rhs: "y4"
      initial_value: 5.0
    y2:
      equation:
        rhs: "y5"
      initial_value: 5.0
    y3:
      equation:
        rhs: "A * a * sigm_y1_y2 - 2.0 * a * y3 - a**2 * y0"
      initial_value: 0.0
    y4:
      equation:
        rhs: "A * a * (mu + a_2 * J * sigm_y0_1 + c_instant + c_delayed) - 2.0 * a * y4 - a**2 * y1"
      initial_value: 0.0
      coupling_variable: true
    y5:
      equation:
        rhs: "B * b * (a_4 * J * sigm_y0_3) - 2.0 * b * y5 - b**2 * y2"
      initial_value: 0.0

  # --- COUPLING INPUTS (multi-coupling: instant + delayed) ---
  coupling_inputs:
    c_instant:
      dimension: 1
    c_delayed:
      dimension: 1

  coupling_terms:
    c_instant: {}
    c_delayed: {}

# --------------------------------------------------------
# COUPLING: DelayedSigmoidalJansenRit
# --------------------------------------------------------
coupling:
  name: DelayedSigmoidalJansenRit
  description: "Sigmoidal Jansen-Rit coupling function with delays"
  parameters:
    G:
      value: 15.0
      description: "Global coupling strength"
      free: true
    cmin:
      value: 0.0
    cmax:
      value: 0.005
      description: "2 * nu_max from TVB default"
    midpoint:
      value: 6.0
    r:
      value: 0.56
  incoming_states: [y1, y2]
  pre_expression:
    rhs: "cmin + (cmax - cmin) / (1.0 + exp(r * (midpoint - (y1 - y2))))"
  post_expression:
    rhs: "G * gx"
  delayed: true

# --------------------------------------------------------
# NETWORK: Structural connectivity with normalization
# --------------------------------------------------------
network:
  label: "Desikan-Killiany 84 regions"
  description: "Structural connectivity from dk_average dataset"
  number_of_regions: 84
  conduction_speed:
    name: conduction_speed
    value: 3.0
    unit: mm/ms
  normalization:
    rhs: "W / W_max"

# --------------------------------------------------------
# INTEGRATION: Heun solver with dt=1.0 ms
# --------------------------------------------------------
integration:
  method: Heun
  step_size: 1.0
  duration: 1000
  transient_time: 20000
  noise:
    additive: true
    parameters:
      sigma:
        value: 0.0001

# --------------------------------------------------------
# OBSERVATIONS: Spectrum via Welch's method
# --------------------------------------------------------
observations:
  - name: spectrum
    label: "Power Spectral Density"
    description: "Power spectral density using Welch's method (subsampled to 100 Hz)"
    source: y0
    equation:
      rhs: "welch(y0[::10], fs=100)"
    parameters:
      fs:
        value: 100
        description: "Sampling frequency after 10x subsampling"

  - name: avg_spectrum
    label: "Average Spectrum"
    description: "Mean power spectrum across all regions"
    source_observation: spectrum
    equation:
      rhs: "mean(Pxx, axis=0)"

  - name: peak_freq
    label: "Peak Frequency"
    description: "Extract peak frequency from average spectrum"
    source_observation: avg_spectrum
    equation:
      rhs: "f[argmax(S)]"

  - name: target_psd
    label: "Target Power Spectra"
    description: >
      Cauchy distribution centered at target frequency for each region.
      Target frequency computed as: f_max - delta_f * (dist - min_dist)
      where f_min=7 Hz, f_max=11 Hz, dist=tract length from visual cortex.
    equation:
      rhs: "cauchy_pdf(f, peak_freqs, gamma=1)"
    parameters:
      f_min:
        value: 7.0
        description: "Minimum frequency at maximum distance"
      f_max:
        value: 11.0
        description: "Maximum frequency at visual cortex"
      gamma:
        value: 1.0
        description: "Cauchy scale parameter (peak width)"

# --------------------------------------------------------
# MODEL FITTING: Target frequencies & correlation loss
# --------------------------------------------------------
optimization:
  - name: spectral_gradient_fit
    label: "Spectral Gradient Fitting"
    description: >
      Fit region-specific a and b parameters to reproduce the MEG frequency
      gradient. Target frequencies range from 11 Hz (visual cortex) to 7 Hz
      (most distant regions from lateral occipital gyrus).

    # Free parameters to optimize (references to local_dynamics.parameters by name)
    free_parameters:
      - a
      - b

    # Target observations for fitting
    targets:
      - spectrum  # Reference to observation above

    # Loss function: 1 - mean correlation between simulated and target PSDs
    loss:
      rhs: "1 - mean(vmap(corrcoef)(predicted_psd, target_psd))"
      label: "Spectral Correlation Loss"

    # Optimizer configuration
    algorithm: adamaxw
    learning_rate: 0.001
    max_iterations: 151

    # Additional optimizer hyperparameters
    hyperparameters:
      has_aux:
        value: 1
        description: "Loss function returns auxiliary data (predicted PSDs)"

# --------------------------------------------------------
# PARAMETER EXPLORATION: Grid search over a and b
# --------------------------------------------------------
explorations:
  - name: frequency_landscape
    label: "Frequency Landscape Exploration"
    description: >
      Grid search over a and b parameters to map the relationship between
      time constants and peak oscillation frequency. Used to understand
      the parameter landscape before optimization.

    # Parameters with grid specifications (use domain with n for grid points)
    parameters:
      - name: a
        domain:
          lo: 0.001
          hi: 0.2
          n: 32
          log_scale: false
      - name: b
        domain:
          lo: 0.001
          hi: 0.2
          n: 32
          log_scale: false

    # Grid combination mode
    mode: product  # Full Cartesian product (32x32 = 1024 points)

    # Parallelization
    n_parallel: 1  # Number of parallel workers for pmap

    # Observable to compute at each grid point
    observable: peak_freq


references:
  - "Mahjoory et al. (2020) eLife 9:e53715 - MEG frequency gradient"
  - "Jansen & Rit (1995) Biol Cybern 73:357-366 - Neural mass model"
"""

# === LOAD FROM STRING ===
exp = SimulationExperiment.from_string(experiment_yaml)
print(f"Loaded: {exp.label}")
print(f"Dynamics: {exp.local_dynamics.name}")
```

## Loading Structural Data

We load the Desikan-Killiany parcellation atlas and structural connectivity data.

```{python}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Load structural connectivity and atlas data"
from tvbo import Network
from tvboptim.data import load_structural_connectivity
import pandas as pd
import nibabel as nib
from mpl_toolkits.axes_grid1 import make_axes_locatable
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import bsplot
import numpy as np
import jax.numpy as jnp

# Load atlas info for visualization
dk_info = pd.read_csv(
    "/Users/leonmartin_bih/work_data/toolboxes/tvboptim/docs/data/dk_average/fs_default_freesurfer_idx.csv"
)
dk = nib.load(
    "/Users/leonmartin_bih/work_data/toolboxes/tvboptim/docs/data/dk_average/aparc+aseg-mni_09c.nii.gz"
)
dk_info.drop_duplicates(subset="freesurfer_idx", inplace=True)

# Load structural connectivity with region labels
weights, lengths, region_labels = load_structural_connectivity(name="dk_average")

weights = weights / jnp.max(weights)
# Attach network to experiment
exp.network = Network.from_matrix(weights, lengths, region_labels)
print(f"Network: {exp.network.number_of_regions} regions")
print(f"Connectivity shape: {exp.network.weights.shape}")
```

## The Jansen-Rit Model

The Jansen-Rit model is a neural mass model that describes the mean activity of interconnected populations of excitatory and inhibitory neurons in a cortical column. It produces realistic alpha-band oscillations.

```{python}
#| label: fig-jr-single
#| fig-cap: "**Single Jansen-Rit oscillator dynamics.** Time series showing characteristic alpha-band oscillations."
ns = exp.execute('tvboptim')
ns.JansenRit(a=0.075, b=0.075, mu=0.15).plot(t1=1000, dt=1)
```

## Background: Resting State MEG

The target frequency gradient is based on empirical observations that brain regions exhibit characteristic peak frequencies that vary with their distance from visual cortex: 11 Hz at visual cortex, decreasing to 7 Hz at the most distant association areas.

```{python}
#| label: fig-distance-visual-cortex
#| fig-cap: "**Distance from visual cortex and target frequency gradient.** Left: Tract length distance from lateral occipital gyrus (visual cortex, outlined in red). Right: Target peak frequencies derived from distance."
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Compute target frequencies from distance"
# Create visual cortex mask
region_labels = np.array(region_labels)
ab_map = np.zeros(dk.shape)
idx = dk_info[dk_info.acronym == "L.LOG"].freesurfer_idx.values[0]
ab_map = np.where(dk.get_fdata() == idx, 1, ab_map)
idx = dk_info[dk_info.acronym == "R.LOG"].freesurfer_idx.values[0]
ab_map = np.where(dk.get_fdata() == idx, 1, ab_map)

# Compute distance from visual cortex (average of L.LOG and R.LOG)
idx_l = np.where(region_labels == "L.LOG")[0]
idx_r = np.where(region_labels == "R.LOG")[0]
dist_from_vc = np.array(np.squeeze(0.5 * (lengths[idx_l, :] + lengths[idx_r, :])))

# Create distance map for visualization
dist_map = np.zeros(dk.shape)
for name, dist in zip(region_labels, dist_from_vc):
    idx = dk_info[dk_info.acronym == name].freesurfer_idx.values[0]
    dist_map = np.where(dk.get_fdata() == idx, dist, dist_map)

# Compute target peak frequencies (linear gradient from distance)
n_nodes = 84
f_min = 7   # Hz at maximum distance
f_max = 11  # Hz at visual cortex
min_dist = dist_from_vc.min()
max_dist = dist_from_vc.max()
delta_f = (f_max - f_min) / (max_dist - min_dist)
peak_freqs = f_max - delta_f * (dist_from_vc - min_dist)

# Create frequency map for visualization
f_map_target = np.zeros_like(dk.get_fdata())
for name, fp in zip(region_labels, peak_freqs):
    idx = dk_info[dk_info.acronym == name].freesurfer_idx.values[0]
    f_map_target = np.where(dk.get_fdata() == idx, fp, f_map_target)

# Plot distance and frequency maps
fig, (ax_gb, ax_freq) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(8.1, 4.05))

mappable_dist = bsplot.brain.glass_brain(
    nib.Nifti1Image(dist_map, dk.affine),
    cmap="cividis", view="horizontal", threshold=0,
    vmin=dist_from_vc.min(), vmax=dist_from_vc.max(), ax=ax_gb,
)
bsplot.anat.plot_img(
    nib.Nifti1Image(ab_map, dk.affine),
    cmap="Greys", threshold=0, ax=ax_gb, view="horizontal",
    intensity_projection="absmax", set_axis_extent=False,
    outline=True, color="red", linewidth=2,
)
ax_gb.axis("off")

mappable_freq = bsplot.brain.glass_brain(
    nib.Nifti1Image(f_map_target, dk.affine),
    cmap="cividis_r", threshold=0, vmin=6.5, vmax=11.5,
    ax=ax_freq, view="horizontal",
)
ax_freq.axis("off")

fig.colorbar(mappable_dist, ax=ax_gb, label="Distance from V1 [mm]")
fig.colorbar(mappable_freq, ax=ax_freq, label="Target Frequency [Hz]")
fig.tight_layout()
```

## Step 1: Run Simulation

```{python}
sim_results = exp.run("tvboptim", mode="simulation")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-simulations
#| fig-cap: "**Network dynamics from transient and quasi-stationary simulations for y0.** Top: First 1000 ms showing transient behavior from random initial conditions. Bottom: Dynamics after the network has settled into a quasi-stationary state."
from matplotlib.colors import Normalize

fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(8.1, 4.05), sharex=True)
t_max = int(1000 / ns.DT)

# First simulation (transient)
time1 = sim_results['result_transient'].time[0:t_max]
data1 = sim_results['result_transient'].data[0:t_max, 0, :]
num_lines = data1.shape[1]
cmap = plt.cm.cividis
mean_values = np.mean(data1, axis=0)
norm = Normalize(vmin=np.min(mean_values), vmax=np.max(mean_values))
for i in range(num_lines):
    color = cmap(norm(mean_values[i]))
    ax1.plot(time1, data1[:, i], color=color, linewidth=0.5)
ax1.text(0.95, 0.95, "Transient", transform=ax1.transAxes, fontsize=12,
         ha='right', va='top', bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.3", facecolor='white', alpha=0.8))
ax1.set_ylabel("y0 [a.u.]")

# Second simulation (updated initial conditions)
time2 = sim_results['result'].time[0:t_max]
data2 = sim_results['result'].data[0:t_max, 0, :]
mean_values = np.mean(data2, axis=0)
norm = Normalize(vmin=np.min(mean_values), vmax=np.max(mean_values))
for i in range(num_lines):
    color = cmap(norm(mean_values[i]))
    ax2.plot(time2, data2[:, i], color=color, linewidth=0.5)
ax2.text(0.95, 0.95, "Updated Initial Conditions", transform=ax2.transAxes, fontsize=12,
         ha='right', va='top', bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.3", facecolor='white', alpha=0.8))
ax2.set_xlabel("Time [ms]")
ax2.set_ylabel("y0 [a.u.]")

plt.tight_layout()
```

## Step 2: Spectral Analysis

```{python}
#| label: fig-initial-spectrum
#| fig-cap: "**Power spectral density of initial network dynamics.** Gray lines show individual region spectra, black line shows network-average spectrum."
f, Pxx = ns.spectrum(sim_results['model_fn'], sim_results['state'])
f, S = ns.avg_spectrum(sim_results['model_fn'], sim_results['state'])
pf = ns.peak_freq(sim_results['model_fn'], sim_results['state'])

fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 1, figsize=(8.1, 3.0375))
ax.plot(f, Pxx.T, linewidth=1, color='k', alpha=0.15)
ax.plot(f, S, linewidth=2, color='k')
ax.set_xlabel('Frequency [Hz]')
ax.set_ylabel('Power')
ax.text(0.95, 0.95, f'Peak @ {pf:.1f} Hz', transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=12,
        ha='right', va='top', bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.3", facecolor='white', alpha=0.8))
ax.set_xlim(0, 20)
ax.set_yscale('log')
plt.tight_layout()
```

## Step 3: Parameter Exploration

```{python}
expl_results = exp.run("tvboptim", mode="exploration")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-parameter-landscape
#| fig-cap: "**Peak frequency landscape across parameter space.** The heatmap shows how the network's dominant frequency varies with the excitatory (a) and inhibitory (b) time constants."
expl_data = expl_results['exploration_results']['frequency_landscape']
grid = expl_data['grid']

pc = grid.collect()
a_vals = pc.dynamics.a
b_vals = pc.dynamics.b
a_min, a_max = min(a_vals), max(a_vals)
b_min, b_max = min(b_vals), max(b_vals)

n = 32
freq_landscape = expl_data['results'].reshape(n, n)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.1, 4.05))
im = ax.imshow(freq_landscape.T,
               cmap='cividis',
               extent=[a_min, a_max, b_min, b_max],
               origin='lower',
               aspect='auto',
               interpolation='none')

ax.scatter(expl_results['state'].dynamics.a, expl_results['state'].dynamics.b, color='k', marker='x', s=50, linewidths=2)
cbar = plt.colorbar(im, label='Peak Frequency [Hz]')
ax.set_xlabel(r'a [ms$^{-1}$]')
ax.set_ylabel(r'b [ms$^{-1}$]')
ax.set_title('Network Dynamics')
plt.tight_layout()
```

## Step 4: Create Target Data

```{python}
#| label: fig-target-spectra
#| fig-cap: "**Comparison of initial and target spectra.** Black lines show current power spectra, blue lines show target spectra with region-specific peak frequencies."
target_PSDs = jnp.vstack([ns.cauchy_pdf(f, fp, 1) for fp in peak_freqs])

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.1, 3.0375))
n_show = 7
for (y, y2) in zip(Pxx[:n_show], target_PSDs[:n_show]):
    ax.plot(f, y, alpha=0.3, color="k", linewidth=1.5)
    ax.plot(f, y2, alpha=0.3, color="royalblue", linewidth=1.5)
ax.set_xlabel('Frequency [Hz]')
ax.set_ylabel('Power')
ax.set_title(f'{n_show} Initial vs Target Power Spectra')
ax.set_xlim(0, 20)
ax.set_yscale('log')
ax.legend(['Initial', 'Target'], loc='upper right')
plt.tight_layout()
```

## Step 5: Optimization

```{python}
opt_results = exp.run("tvboptim", mode="optimization", target_data=target_PSDs)
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-optimized-params
#| fig-cap: "**Optimized parameters overlaid on the frequency landscape.** Each white dot represents the fitted (a, b) parameters for one brain region."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.1, 5.207))
im = ax.imshow(freq_landscape.T,
               cmap='cividis',
               extent=[a_min, a_max, b_min, b_max],
               origin='lower',
               aspect='auto')

a_fit = opt_results['fitted_params'].dynamics.a.value
b_fit = opt_results['fitted_params'].dynamics.b.value
ax.scatter(a_fit, b_fit, color='white', s=20, marker='o',
           edgecolors='black', linewidths=1, zorder=5, alpha=0.7)

cbar = plt.colorbar(im, label='Peak Frequency [Hz]')
ax.set_xlabel(r'a [ms$^{-1}$]')
ax.set_ylabel(r'b [ms$^{-1}$]')
plt.tight_layout()
```

## Frequency Maps

```{python}
#| label: fig-frequency-maps
#| fig-cap: "**Comparison of initial and fitted peak frequencies.** Left: Before optimization. Right: After optimization matching target gradient."
_, PSDs_fit = ns.spectrum(opt_results['model_fn'], opt_results['fitted_params'])
_, PSDs_init = ns.spectrum(opt_results['model_fn'], opt_results['state'])

peak_freqs_fitted = np.array([f[np.argmax(psd)] for psd in PSDs_fit])
peak_freqs_init = np.array([f[np.argmax(psd)] for psd in PSDs_init])

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(8.1, 3.5))

axes[0].scatter(peak_freqs, peak_freqs_init, alpha=0.6, s=20)
axes[0].plot([7, 11], [7, 11], 'k--', linewidth=1)
axes[0].set_xlabel('Target Peak Frequency [Hz]')
axes[0].set_ylabel('Initial Peak Frequency [Hz]')
axes[0].set_title('Before Optimization')
axes[0].set_xlim(6.5, 11.5)
axes[0].set_ylim(6.5, 11.5)

axes[1].scatter(peak_freqs, peak_freqs_fitted, alpha=0.6, s=20)
axes[1].plot([7, 11], [7, 11], 'k--', linewidth=1)
axes[1].set_xlabel('Target Peak Frequency [Hz]')
axes[1].set_ylabel('Fitted Peak Frequency [Hz]')
axes[1].set_title('After Optimization')
axes[1].set_xlim(6.5, 11.5)
axes[1].set_ylim(6.5, 11.5)

plt.tight_layout()
```

## Brain Frequency Maps

```{python}
# | label: fig-brain-frequency-maps
# | fig-cap: "**Comparison of initial, target, and fitted frequency gradients.** Left: Initial homogeneous peak frequency. Center: Target frequency gradient from visual cortex. Right: Fitted peak frequencies after optimization."

from matplotlib.colors import Normalize

f_map_init = np.zeros_like(dk.get_fdata())
f_map_fitted = np.zeros_like(dk.get_fdata())

for i, name in enumerate(region_labels):
    idx = dk_info[dk_info.acronym == name].freesurfer_idx.values[0]
    f_map_init = np.where(dk.get_fdata() == idx, peak_freqs_init[i], f_map_init)
    f_map_fitted = np.where(dk.get_fdata() == idx, peak_freqs_fitted[i], f_map_fitted)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(12, 4))

norm = Normalize(vmin=0, vmax=12)

mappable_init = bsplot.brain.glass_brain(
    nib.Nifti1Image(f_map_init, dk.affine),
    cmap="cividis_r",
    view="horizontal",
    threshold=0,
    norm=norm,
    ax=axes[0],
)
axes[0].set_title("Initial (Homogeneous)")
axes[0].axis("off")

mappable_target = bsplot.brain.glass_brain(
    nib.Nifti1Image(f_map_target, dk.affine),
    cmap="cividis_r",
    view="horizontal",
    threshold=0,
    norm=norm,
    ax=axes[1],
)
axes[1].set_title("Target (Gradient)")
axes[1].axis("off")

mappable_fitted = bsplot.brain.glass_brain(
    nib.Nifti1Image(f_map_fitted, dk.affine),
    cmap="cividis_r",
    view="horizontal",
    threshold=0,
    norm=norm,
    ax=axes[2],
)
axes[2].set_title("Fitted")
axes[2].axis("off")

fig.colorbar(mappable_fitted, ax=axes[2], label="Peak Frequency [Hz]", shrink=0.8)
fig.colorbar(mappable_target, ax=axes[1], label="Peak Frequency [Hz]", shrink=0.8)
fig.colorbar(mappable_init, ax=axes[0], label="Peak Frequency [Hz]", shrink=0.8)

fig.tight_layout()
```
